title: WeilConjectures.zetaSeries_rational (Dwork rationality)
statement: Let $k$ be a finite field with $q=\#k$ elements, let $X$ be a scheme, and let $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ be locally of finite type and quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. For $n\geq1$, let $F_{q^n}=\operatorname{FiniteField.galoisExtension}(k,n)$ be the splitting field over $k$ of $U^{q^n}-U$. Let $N_n=f.\mathrm{pointCount}(n)$ be the number of $k$-morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}F_{q^n}\to X$, namely morphisms whose composite with $f$ is the map induced by $k\to F_{q^n}$, with value $0$ if this set is infinite. Define $Z(X,t)=f.\mathrm{zetaSeries}=\exp(\sum_{n\geq1}N_nt^n/n)\in\mathbf Q[[t]]$ using substitution into the formal exponential [sk-def-zeta, def-weil-formal-power-series]. An integral polynomial is viewed in $\mathbf Q[[t]]$ by first mapping its coefficients to $\mathbf Q[t]$ and then taking its power series with the same coefficients [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map, def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series]. Then there are $P,Q\in\mathbf Z[t]$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring] with $Q(0)=1$ [def-weil-polynomial-coefficient] such that $Z(X,t)Q(t)=P(t)$ in $\mathbf Q[[t]]$. No smoothness, properness or separatedness is assumed.

proof.text: By [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], the hypotheses on $f:X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ say exactly that $X$ is of finite type over $k$. Use $k_0=k$ and $q=\#k$ in [sk-def-zeta], taking its stated splitting-field model of $\mathbf F_{q^n}$. Its point set consists of the $k$-morphisms $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf F_{q^n}\to X$, with count zero when that set is infinite, exactly as in the definition of $f.\mathrm{pointCount}$. Its series is the formal exponential of $\sum_{n\geq1}N_nT^n/n$. The comparator substitutes into the same exponential the series with coefficient $0$ at degree $0$ and $N_n/n$ at degree $n\geq1$. Thus $Z(X,T)$ in the theorem below is precisely $f.\mathrm{zetaSeries}$; the unused degree-zero splitting-field value contributes no term.

source.place: Splitting-field model, point-count display and exponential display; checked against lean/Comparator/Weil/Definitions.lean:67-103 and the hypotheses of Challenge.lean:80-84.

proof.text: Apply [sk-thm-weil1] to this finite-type $k$-scheme. Its first clause gives $A,B\in\mathbf Z[T]$, $B(0)=1$, and $B(T)Z(X,T)=A(T)$ in $\mathbf Q[[T]]$. Set $P=A$ and $Q=B$. By [def-weil-coefficientwise-ring-hom-map], the integral polynomials in that identity are mapped to $\mathbf Q[T]$ along $\mathbf Z\to\mathbf Q$, $c\mapsto c\cdot1$. By [def-weil-polynomial-as-power-series] they are then regarded as power series with the same coefficients, and $B(0)$ is their constant coefficient. Consequently the asserted equation is $f.\mathrm{zetaSeries}\cdot(Q.\mathrm{map}(\operatorname{Int.castRingHom}\mathbf Q))=P.\mathrm{map}(\operatorname{Int.castRingHom}\mathbf Q)$ in $\mathbf Q[[T]]$, after commuting the two factors on the left. Also $Q.\mathrm{coeff}(0)=B(0)=1$. These witnesses prove every clause of the item.

theorem zetaSeries_rational [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f] :
    ∃ P Q : Polynomial ℤ, Q.coeff 0 = 1 ∧
      f.zetaSeries * (Q.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) : PowerSeries ℚ) =
        (P.map (Int.castRingHom ℚ) : PowerSeries ℚ)
